checks.name: central_question_resolved
checks.evidence: The book asks whether every odiyan, including the queen's guard, can be freed while Varanad keeps its night-guard against the Thurai. Ch 24: twenty-six of the thirty guards and most of the forty self-name, and their crown leaves burn in the queen's lap. Ch 25-26: the bound pairs hold the shelf. Ch 29: the Thurai, 'short of captains and denied the shelf', withdraw and ask for a truce, and Chathu's forty pages are shown to be plain ink with no power. Ch 30: the last unbound members self-name (Lata to Usha, Kamalakshi to Janu). Ch 31: the queen signs the charter ('No page, leaf or ledger of any member shall be held by the crown'), the last three guard pages are read aloud to their owners and the crown leaf is burned. Ch 32: the Thurai fleet sails under open truce. Only the series hinge stays open: the unledgered rogue and the sea lords' offer to hire the Company.

checks.name: clues_paid_off
checks.evidence: Every clue pays off on the page or is a series thread. C01 (ch 7) pays off in ch 16. C02 (ch 3) pays off in ch 16 ('Chathu's rat-eaten page and Kamalakshi's question snap into place'). C03 (ch 13, echoed ch 22) pays off in ch 29 ('It's plain ink'). C04 (ch 2) pays off in ch 16 ('Spread for what the realm sees. Folded for what it needn't'). C05 (ch 2) pays off in ch 24, when Usha names herself to the queen. C06 (ch 1) pays off in ch 7 (Ponni, Ammini). C07 (ch 7), C08 (ch 8) and C17 (ch 13) pay off in ch 29: the record laid before the queen, and the note 'Written off. Paid in full. C.' C09 (ch 2) pays off in ch 25 and 28 (strike used once, hand lost). C10 (ch 5) pays off in ch 27 ('Dev? Keep the light there'). C11 (ch 9 and 12) pays off in ch 26, when Thankam operates. C14 (ch 4) pays off in ch 11 ('Refugees are the reason I can write it down'). C16 (ch 12) pays off in ch 16 (Usha told the queen). C18 (ch 10) pays off as a lamp callback in ch 27-28. C20 (ch 1) pays off in ch 32 (boat named Kirri). C21 (ch 2) pays off in ch 30 (writ read aloud and given to Rema). C22 (ch 10) pays off in ch 19 (the missed noon signal explained). C23 (ch 17) pays off in ch 29 (Rema arrives). Two payoffs are weaker than their outline slots. C15's ch 31 payoff is the groves going 'under the map of Pachan'; the noon trees are not named again. C19's clearest payoff is ch 22 (Parukutty's petition); ch 31 only echoes it in passing. C12 and C13 are series threads.

checks.name: midpoint_reversal
checks.evidence: Ch 16 is the midpoint. The queen shows a fresh resin-ink page for Usha ('You carried away paper. You can't carry away what I saw'). This recasts the first half: stealing the pages never freed anyone. She owns the folded bird as her private hand, and she prices Devan's old office ('I give Devan back Kettamala') against Neela's answer. The romance turns on it: 'The only freedom I have ever had is the one that bleeds when he does.' The missed noon signal and Devan's unilateral refusal of the offer (ch 17) then produce the breach-and-repair in ch 20.

checks.name: heroine_belief_change
checks.evidence: In ch 1 Neela 'wrote her own name there... hers last', stood at the back, and believed freedom meant belonging to no one. In ch 28 she says 'The queen says the first name binds me to the Company's vote, whatever the hands decide. If they vote against me, I go with it... For twenty-one years I answered to a number. I wanted to be no one's... It was a very quiet cage.' Then she writes first, by daylight before every witness: '*Indu, called Neela, of Nellimala and Kettamala.*' The belief is stated in ch 24 ('It is not belonging to no one. It is choosing who you're tied to, and being able to walk away, and staying') and enacted in ch 31 with 'Bound by choice.'

checks.name: real_loss
checks.evidence: Ch 27: Vellan dies holding Kamalakshi's carved bird ('It's light... I can see the steps'). He stays dead and is carried down on a door. Ch 28: Thankam says 'The hand won't come back.' Devan answers 'Then it won't', and the killing strike is gone for good. In ch 32 he still trains left-handed with his arm in the sash. The dead on Kandan's tile (Biju, Sankaran, Lekha, Orma, Kani, Swathi, Sreedhar) also stay lost.

checks.name: love_interest_goal
checks.evidence: Devan's goal is to hold the Monkey Pass for the hill villages without office or crown leave. It is set in ch 1 ('I mean to go down and hold the gorge'), hardens in ch 2 on reading 'as they always have', and drives ch 5, 8, 11, 14, 19, 23 and 25. In ch 17 he refuses to buy the pass with Neela's answer: 'I will hold the pass with whoever chooses to stand.' A second goal, getting the payment writ seen in daylight, pays off in ch 30 ('I don't want a lever. I want it seen').

checks.name: series_hinge
checks.evidence: Ch 32 opens a bigger question. A Thurai envoy under truce cloth asks to hire the Night Company. Beside him walks a scarred odiyan whose wrists smell of 'salt. Sweet, dry clove-bark', and Neela realises 'He was in none of it': someone is making odiyans outside any Resin House ledger, and the sea lords hold him. Koman reports the long river shape watching the road again. The book ends on the Company's first open vote: 'We vote at noon.'

series_threads.thread: Salt-and-clove-bark resin on scarred Thurai wrists, found on the sleeper at Nellimala (ch 6) and the dead scout (ch 8). Ch 32 resolves it into the hinge: an unledgered rogue odiyan travelling with the sea lords' envoy, so a second, unknown maker of odiyans exists across the sea.

The long, low river shape that no Company scent matches (ch 17). It watches the shelf (ch 20), drags Thurai wounded from the river without fighting (ch 26) and watches the reopened pass road (ch 32). Its nature and allegiance are left for book 2.

summary: The book meets all seven structural promises. It answers its own central question through the naming dusk, the plain-ink reveal, the charter and the Thurai withdrawal. It lands a midpoint mirror in ch 16 that recasts both the theft and the romance. It proves Neela's belief change by her first-name, daylight binding in ch 28, set against chalking her name last in ch 1. It keeps Vellan's death and Devan's hand as permanent losses, gives Devan an outward goal (the pass), and ends on a hinge about an unledgered Thurai rogue. All 23 outline clues are paid off or logged as series threads (C12, C13). Two payoffs are softer than their outline slots: C15 resolves through the grove map rather than the noon trees, and C19 is fully demonstrated in ch 22 rather than ch 31. The owner may want to tighten these. Minor continuity to check, outside these checks: ch 22's count of eight guards riding with the queen sits awkwardly with Lata already being at the shelf. Ch 29's 'twelve hundred Thurai or more' differs from the fourteen hundred used elsewhere.
